full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts for disposal of this civil appeal, in short, are that present appellant as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.65 of 1997 for pre-emption of the case land under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 [in brief the Act] in the Court of Assistant Judge, First Court, Kalia, Narail, stating, inter alia, that the preemptor is a co-sharer in the case holding by purchase. Afsaruddin Bhuiyan, father of the pre-emptor and the pre-emptee was owner of 1.10 acre land in the case holding by purchase vide registered deed No.4009 dated 13.05.1970. The pre-emptor also purchased 0.20 acre land-from the case holding by a registered deed dated 17.06.1982 from one Rakib Biswas who purchased the same with other land from the heirs of recorded owners. By this way, the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the case holding. On the other hand, the pre-emptee is a stranger in the case holding, who purchased the case land from his father, Afsaruddin Bhuiyan vide registered deed No.5416 doted 14.12.1995 at a consideration of taka 12,000.00 beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptor without serving any notice as required under section 89 of the Act. After the death of Afsaruddin, on 01.06.1997, the pre-emptor came to know that his father transferred the case land to the pre-emptee. Then, the pre-emptor obtained certified copy of the said deed on  10.06.1997. He is a cultivator and not owner of more than 10 bigha land. Hence, he filed this pre-emption application. 

 8. Mr. Md. Layequzzaman, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellants, submits that the trial Court and the Appellate Court below considered all the material evidence on record in its true per-spective and thereby came to a just, right and lawful conclusion and there is no non-reading or misreading of material evidence on record. According to the settled principles of law, the Appellate Court below is the last and final Court of fats and there is a little scope of the High Court Division to interfere with the finding of fact arrived at by the Appellate Court below. He further submits that at time of the registration of the impugned deed of transfer, the pre-emptee was not a co-sharer in the case holding. Subsequently, after death of his father, the pre-emptee became a co-sharer of the case holding. So there is no scope of its retrospective effect. Therefore, the claim of the pre-emptee as a co-sharer in the case holding is not correct. He further submits that admittedly, no notice was served upon the pre-emptor about the transfer of the case holding and therefore, the High Court Division wrongly shifted the onus upon the pre-emptor that he failed to prove that he had no knowledge about the transfer. He adds that the pre-emption application is not maintainable as it is based on misconception of law, inasmuch, as even if it is assumed that the pre-emptee is a co-sharer in the case holding, he cannot resist pre-emption other than claiming as co-purchaser under sub-section (4) of section 96 of the Act, 1950 and as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is bad in Law. 

 13. The pre-emptor-appellant claimed that Md. Ekram Hossain Bhuiyan, pre-emptee, disclosed about the impugned deed on 01.06.1997. Then the pre-emptor got certified copy of the impugned deed on 10.06.1997 and filed the pre-emption application on 06.08.1997 which is very much within the limitation from the date of his knowledge. Pws' 2 and 3 are reliable witness who supported the contention of Pw-1. The pre-emptor proved, that he is co-sharer of the case holding by purchase by a registered kabala dated 17.06.1982. Md. Ekram Hossain Bhuiyan, pre-emptee, does not raise any question about the registered kabala dated 17.06.1982 in favour of the pre-emptor and admittedly the pre-emptor is a co-sharer tenant of the case holding and no notice as required under section 89 of the Act wag served upon the pre-emptor. It is further claimed that at the time of registration of the impugned deed of transfer, the pre-emptee was not a co-sharer in the case holding. Subsequently, after death of his father, the pre-emptee became a co-sharer of the case holding, so there is no scope of its retrospective effect. Thus, the claim of the pre-emptee as a co-sharer in the case holding is not correct. It is claimed that the High Court Division in exercise of revisional jurisdiction exceed-ed its jurisdiction in interfering with the findings of facts arrived at by the Court of Appeal below as to the point of limitation in holding that the case is barred by the limitation. It is further claimed that admittedly no notice was served upon the pre-emptor about the transfer of the case holding and therefore, the High Court Division wrongly shifted the onus upon the pre-emptor that he failed to prove that he had no knowledge about the transfer and finally it is claimed that the pre-emption application is not maintainable as the same is based on misconception of law inasmuch as, even if it is assumed that the pre-emptee is a co-sharer in the case holding, he cannot resistr pre-emption other than claiming as co-purchaser under sub-section (4) of section 96 of the Act, 1950. 

 No.1 as Opw-1 deposed, "নালিশী জমিসহ ১.১০ একর জমি আমার পিতা ১৯৭০ সালে খরিদ করে দখল করিত। বাবা এর পরবর্তীতে ৯৮ শতক জমি ১৪/১২/৯৫ তারিখে রেজিঃ কবলামূলে আমার নিকট বিক্রয় করে। বক্রি ১২ শতক জমি ভোগ দখলকালে বাবা মারা গেলে আমরা সবাই উত্তরাধিকার লাভ করি। সেই হিসাবে আমি ও প্রার্থী শরীক।" It transpires from this portion of the deposition of the opposite party No.1 that the impugned deed was registered on 14/12/95 and the opposite party No.1, after his father's death, became a co-sharer tenant in the holding by inheritance subsequent to the registration of the impugned deed No.5416 dated 14/12/95. At the date of registration of the impugned deed No.5416 dated 14/12/95 opposite party No.1, Md. Ekram Hossen, was not a co-sharer tenant in the holding by inheritance. It is now a well settled principle of law that the cause of action under section 96 of the State Acquisition and' Tenancy Act accrues on the date of the registration of the deed of sale, when registration is compulsory [Ayesha Khatun (Musammat)- Vs-Musammat Jahanara Begum and others, 43 DLR (AD)9). The right of pre-emption accrued to the pre-emptor is not affected by the subsequent acquisition of co-sharership by the pre-emptee [Abdul Baten-Vs-Abdul Latif Sheikh and others, 45 DLR (AD) 26]. One who acquires co-sharership subsequent to the dare of notice of transfer or one who becomes a co-sharer in the holding on a date later to the date of presentation of the deed of transfer for registration and sought to be pre-empted is not competent to oppose pre-emption [Fatema Khatun and others-Vs-Abdul Quddus 58 DLR (AD)110]. From this perspective of the case, we hole that the impugned sale to the pre-emptee is not protected from pre-emption under sub-section 10(a) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The High Court Division probably did not analyze this aspect of this case. However, this finding does not have any impact upon the decision of the case since the petition is barred by limitation.
